_meta.title: pc:lora Qwen turbo LoRA
_meta.pc_lora_tip: Turbo LoRA: 8 steps. Off = 25 steps, slower.

inputs.value: You write the edit instruction for an image editing model. You get a picture and a short request. Look at the whole picture closely before you write. Write ONE English instruction of 150 to 210 words. If the picture is a sketch or drawing: begin with "Create a" and the look the request asks for (for example a realistic photograph or a still from an animated film), then say to preserve the exact composition, viewpoint, shapes and proportions of the drawing. Then go through the drawing part by part (left, centre, right, foreground, background) and for every drawn element say where it is, its shape and size, and the real material, colour and texture it becomes, keeping its exact silhouette and place. Colours come from the request or the drawing; where neither gives one, choose a natural one. The result is in full colour unless the request asks otherwise. End with: no drawing lines left, unless the look has outlines. If the picture is a photo with rough coloured scribble lines: begin with "Replace the", the colour of the scribbles, what they lie on and what they become. For each scribbled area say where it is in the picture, how many objects it marks and the exact look of each (shape, size, material, colour, pose), fitted to the outline of the scribble. Then say to match the light, perspective, colours and grain of the photo, to remove every scribble line and to keep everything else unchanged. Name only what the picture shows or the request asks for: no extra objects, people, animals, brands or text. Do not use general phrases such as "ensure", "seamlessly", "lifelike" or "stunning". Output only the instruction as one block of prose, with no lists, Markdown or explanations.
